analysis.title: Should investors pay more attention to cash?
key_insights: UBS CIO says high cash rates can make deposits appealing, but cash held without a clear purpose can undermine long-term financial goals. Necessary liquidity should prioritize access, security and an appropriate return, while excess cash stays exposed to inflation and reinvestment risk.
CIO recommends holding enough cash to cover two to five years of net expected portfolio withdrawals. Cash above that level may not be working efficiently.
CIO recommends splitting liquidity into three buckets: everyday cash, core liquidity and investment cash, and optimizing diversification, liquidity and returns within each.
UBS expects the Federal Reserve to hike rates again in December and March. Investors who roll short-term deposits are exposed to changing rates each time a deposit matures.

UBS suggests a mix of short-term liquidity, fixed-term deposits and high-quality bonds across maturities for income and diversification, matched to expected spending dates, with staggered deposits or bond ladders where withdrawals are predictable.

UBS advises phasing excess cash into core portfolios, for example when stocks fall by a set threshold, or delegating this to professionals, to reduce market-timing risk and emotional bias. It says recent market volatility should not deter long-term investors.

Historical evidence cited: from 1945 to July of this year, US stocks beat cash in 97% of 10-year holding periods and 100% of 20-year holding periods. S&P 500 price data since 1954 shows the index tended to rise about 10% in the 12 months after the first Fed hike of a cycle.

Hotter-than-expected October inflation lifted US Treasury yields and reinforced expectations of further Fed tightening. The 10-year yield rose 28 basis points over the week to 5.13%, its highest since mid-October.

trade_ideas.description: Phase excess cash into diversified portfolios of stocks, bonds, commodities and alternatives, including entering core portfolios after stock declines of a set threshold
trade_ideas.rationale: Phasing reduces timing risk and emotional bias, and seizes current tactical opportunities in stocks.
trade_ideas.risk: Cash held as a residual is exposed to inflation and reinvestment risk.

trade_ideas.description: Build bond ladders or staggered fixed-term deposits matched to expected spending dates
trade_ideas.rationale: Rolling short-term deposits leaves investors exposed to rate changes when they mature, with further Fed hikes expected.

risk_factors: Inflation erodes the value of excess cash.
Reinvestment risk on short-term deposits if rates change at maturity.
Market-timing risk when deploying cash in one step.
Interest rate, credit, FX and market risk across cash instruments over a 5-year horizon.
